title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## WM-LOCO Humanoid Visual Locomotion

### The Breakthrough
WM-LOCO couples a recurrent world model with a PPO policy, using a single depth camera and onboard proprioception to predict near‑future observations for foot‑placement decisions. The approach eliminates explicit foothold labeling and, when deployed on a real Unitree G1 humanoid, achieves a 93.3% success rate across gaps, stepping stones, and narrow stairs.

### The Caveats
The work never isolates the world‑model’s contribution, providing no ablation study to verify that the reported locomotion gains truly stem from the predictive model rather than other factors.

## SA-WAM Depth-Aware World Action Model

### The Breakthrough
SA‑WAM repurposes a frozen video diffusion backbone and adds a nonlinear depth encoding that fits the VAE tokenizer’s bounded domain, enabling joint RGB‑depth‑action prediction. The model attains state‑of‑the‑art results on RoboCasa and LIBERO‑Plus simulated benchmarks and shows strong performance gains on a real UR5 arm in randomized settings.

### The Caveats
The paper lists no direct comparison to existing baselines, leaving the reported gains unverified.

## HINT Human Intent for Long-Horizon Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
HINT injects sparse human intent into long‑horizon manipulation via semantic highlighting and attention‑prior injection, without adding trainable parameters. Experiments on three long‑horizon tasks and out‑of‑distribution variants show notable gains in intent understanding, task progress, and overall success for two foundation policies.

### The Caveats
The reported gains are demonstrated solely in simulation, with no real‑world robot experiments, so the method’s practical effectiveness remains unproven.

## World-Model Rollout Evaluation Study

### The Breakthrough
The study quantifies the correlation between offline rollout error and closed‑loop tracking error on a differential‑drive robot, finding a Spearman ρ of 0.923 for replay versus 0.774 for 20‑step rollouts, and reduces EKF‑anchored RMSE from 1.72 m to 1.06 m under combined sensor outages.

### The Caveats
Findings are limited to a single simulated robot, with no real‑world hardware validation, so applicability to physical systems is unclear.

## Tesla Cybercab Camera‑Only Robotaxi

### The Breakthrough
Tesla’s Cybercab runs a camera‑only version of the Full Self‑Driving neural net, removes radar and lidar, adds Starlink connectivity for remote operator intervention, and is marketed below $30,000 to enable mass deployment of robotaxis.

### The Caveats
The safety claim rests on a public‑road rollout with no formal, independent evaluation or crash data, so its superiority over lidar‑equipped fleets remains unproven.

## EgoLens Browser 3D Dataset Explorer

### The Breakthrough
EgoLens is an open‑source TypeScript app that auto‑detects dataset layouts and renders LiDAR point clouds, camera images, and semantic overlays from Waymo, nuScenes, and Argoverse 2 directly in WebGL, with a “Teachable Lens” that lets agents declaratively add new sensor formats without server code.

### The Caveats
The tool is demonstrated only with a live demo on example datasets and provides no performance, scalability, or user‑study measurements, so its practicality for larger or real‑world AV data remains unproven.

## Mireye Physical‑World AI Agent API

### The Breakthrough
Mireye aggregates 366 public‑record fields for every U.S. address into a unified schema, offers deterministic geometry tools, and provides on‑demand indexing that validates and adds new fields within a day, enabling AI agents to query up‑to‑date physical‑world data.

### The Caveats
The announcement provides no quantitative accuracy metrics or real‑world robot deployment evidence, so the claimed nationwide coverage remains unverified.

## Canadarm IEEE 300th Milestone

### The Breakthrough
The Canadarm delivered six‑degree‑of‑freedom manipulation in zero‑gravity using a 400 kg, 15 m titanium‑graphite‑epoxy arm, handling payloads up to 266 000 kg via hand controllers and video feedback, marking a historic achievement in space robotics.

### The Caveats
The announcement provides no independent verification or context for the IEEE milestone designation, so the significance of the claim cannot be independently assessed.

### Priority
WM‑LOCO shows how a predictive world model can be integrated into real humanoid hardware to dramatically improve locomotion on complex terrain, making it the most actionable development today.

### One action
Visit the WM‑LOCO repository and try the provided depth‑camera locomotion stack on your own robot platform.

### What to watch
Multiple world‑model papers appear: WM‑LOCO leverages a recurrent latent model for real‑time locomotion, SA‑WAM embeds depth into a diffusion model for manipulation, while the rollout‑evaluation study probes how offline metrics reflect closed‑loop performance. Together they signal a shift toward using predictive models not just for planning but also for benchmarking and debugging real‑world robots.
